claims: [P1] Quota poll only at start and every 500 (`tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:1058`): with no `X-Intel-Datapoints-Remaining` header, `quota.remaining` only changes at startup (`:859`) and every 500 addresses, so the check at `:1000` reads a stale number and the run can use up the trial quota, stopping only on the 402/403 halt
Usage and Limit headers are also never turned into a Remaining value (`:541-542`)
[P1] A numeric flag with no value falls back silently (`:112-126`): `--limit --no-refresh` or a trailing `--limit` becomes `Infinity`, and a trailing `--quota-floor` becomes 50

[P2] Capped discovery source only warns (`:284-287`): a source that hits `capped: true` logs a warning and then passes the abort gate at `:300`, which only looks at `failedSources`, contradicting the header comment at `:15-17`

The tier2 tag-ordering fix gets undone when the new tags are merged with the existing entry (`tier2-light-forensic.mjs:671-682`): existing tags come first in `new Set([...existingEntry.tags, ...derived.tags]).slice(0, 20)`, so addresses tier1 labeled with about 14+ Arkham ids lose their `ctp:*`/`type:contract` tags

The new circuit breaker's "resumes the queue" message isn't true for the addresses that tripped it (`tier1-bulk-enrich.mjs:1043-1047`, `:809-813`, `:966`): failed addresses get `{address, error}` progress lines that resume treats as processed, so the 10 addresses behind the halt, and every address whose 429 retry failed, are skipped forever

judge_reasoning.3845594538: Not identified. The review never says flushWrites splices the batch out before the network call and so loses writes on an Upstash failure. Its circuit-breaker point is about resume skipping errored addresses.
judge_reasoning.3845596185: Identified. The review confirms that a source returning capped: true only warns and still passes the abort gate, which checks only failedSources.
judge_reasoning.3845603922: Not identified. The review clears run.sh's grep and never mentions prefix matching of tfvars keys.
judge_reasoning.3845603940: Not identified. The review notices slice-before-dedup but treats it as correct parity with the shared helper, not as a defect.
judge_reasoning.3845607361: Identified. Finding 2 says tier2's write path puts existingEntry.tags first and slices to 20, so tier1's populatedTags push out the ctp:/type: tags ordered at :395.
judge_reasoning.3845618202: Not identified. The review raises the tag-ordering loss only for tier2's write path. It does not flag tier1's refresh buildWriteEntry putting fresh tags ahead of existing forensic tags.

1.why: quota.remaining is only set by noteQuotaHeaders (needs the Remaining header, :543-546) or logIntelUsage, which runs at start and every INTEL_USAGE_EVERY=500 (:1058), so the default floor of 50 checked at :1000 can be overrun by hundreds of lookups between polls

2.why: noteQuotaHeaders stores usage/limit (:541-542) but only sets quota.remaining from the Remaining header, and never computes limit-usage, so a per-request Usage/Limit pair never refreshes the brake

3.why: flagValue returns undefined when the next arg is missing or starts with '--' (:117), and numericFlag then returns the fallback without an error (:127), so --limit becomes Infinity and --quota-floor becomes 50. That goes against the hard-fail intent in the comment at :119-123

4.why: Same as the known HARD_PAGE_CAP defects: at :284-287 capped only logs a warning, and the abort at :300 only checks failedSources

5.why: Same as the known tier2-light-forensic.mjs:395 'Preserve Tier 2 tags when merging capped labels': existing tags go first in the Set and then .slice(0,20) at :671-682

6.why: The resume loader (:805-813) adds any line with an address to processed, including {address,error} lines written at :1043-1047, so the addresses that trip the new circuit breaker (:966 exit) are skipped on re-run even though the message says the progress file 'resumes the queue'
